To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PbO is a good candidate as a stabilizing agent of PbO in cement mortars.
the release of lead from stabilized/solidified samples is a surface phenomenon.
the release of lead during leaching test depends on initial concentration of lead and on leaching time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for stabilization and immobilization of lead.
the evaluation of the performance of PbO stabilization/solidification process by the toxicity characteristic leaching procedure test.
the evaluation of the performance of the Stabilization / Solidification of PbO in cement mortars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stabilization/solidification process was very effective and that the lead is not released from the matrix.
the process of Solidified / Stabilization is effective for lead compounds, and can be used for the immobilization of this pollutant.
the process of stabilization/solidification is effective and can be considered as a good alternative solution for PbO hazardous waste.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of cement as a binder in the solidification/stabilization of lead oxide is an effective process.
the process of stabilization/solidification of lead by hydraulic binder (CEM II 42.5) is an effective method to reduce the mobility and the leaching of the pollutant.
PbO can be stabilized in cementitious matrices, and that the release process of lead is a surface phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stabilization/solidification process of Pb by cement is a viable option for hazardous waste disposal.
the use of cement is a viable and effective method to stabilize/solidify PbO in an acidic medium.
the release of the Pb is controlled by the kinetics of the dissolution/precipitation of PbO and that it depends on the initial concentration and the time of leach.
